key_insight: Failures that are rare, complex, or adversarially hidden often only become visible when multiple agent traces are analyzed together; by scoring and searching over sets of traces (not just individual ones), auditors can reliably surface these cross-trace safety violations.
problem_solved: Detecting safety violations in large collections of agent traces where failures are sparse, compositional, or intentionally concealed — situations where per-trace judges miss problems that only emerge across multiple executions.
method: Formulate cross-trace detection: evaluate candidate sets of traces with an aggregated failure score instead of per-trace labels.
Scalable search: use sampling, pruning, and targeted search heuristics to find small groups of traces that maximize the failure score across a huge trace corpus.
Robust validation: prioritize findings that are statistically or semantically robust to rare and adversarial patterns, and provide human-in-the-loop verification for high-risk cases.
impact: Enables auditors and ML teams to find hard-to-detect, multi-trace safety failures that would otherwise slip past per-trace checks, improving model auditing, risk assessment, and mitigation for deployed agents.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: many traces → cross-trace scorer/search → flagged trace-sets → human review
Before/After example: per-trace view showing 'no failure' vs grouped-trace view revealing the hidden violation
Heatmap or rarity chart: frequency of failures vs size of trace-set needed to detect them
Flowchart or icon set illustrating scalable search strategies (sampling, pruning, heuristics) and human-in-the-loop validation
paper_title: Detecting Safety Violations Across Many Agent Traces
paper_authors: Adam Stein, Davis Brown, Hamed Hassani, Mayur Naik, Eric Wong
